## Why CC Switch? AI coding tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI each have their own configuration format. Switching API providers means hand-editing JSON, TOML, YAML, or `.env` files, and MCP, Skills, and prompts have to be maintained separately in every tool. **CC Switch** brings all of this into a single desktop app: pick a preset, enter your key, and switch in one click. Switching replaces only the connection details — endpoint, key, and model — so plugins, hooks, MCP, and comments you added yourself stay as they are. - **One App, Twelve Tools** — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi, MiniMax Code, Kimi Code, and Oh My Pi - **No More Manual Editing** — 90+ provider presets including AWS Bedrock, NVIDIA NIM, and community relays - **Direct, Routing, or Aggregation — Your Choice** — Direct connects the tool straight to the provider; Routing forwards requests through your machine, converting API formats and failing over automatically, so you can use GPT in Claude Code and Claude in Codex; Aggregation puts models from several providers into one model list in Claude Code or Codex, and each request goes to the provider of the model you pick - **Centralized MCP, Skills & Prompts** — Add MCP servers and Skills once, then choose which tools to sync them to; prompts are maintained separately for each tool - **Sessions You Can Read** — Turns each tool's session logs into a reading view: what each turn did, which files changed, and which step failed, all at a glance - **Usage & Quotas at a Glance** — Track token usage and spending even without local routing; remaining subscription quota and account balances show right on provider cards and in the tray - **Cross-Platform** — Native desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux, built with Tauri 2 ## Screenshots

## Download & Installation ### System Requirements - **Windows**: Windows 10 and above - **macOS**: macOS 12 (Monterey) and above - **Linux**: x86_64 or ARM64 with glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1 — e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, and recent Fedora releases; RHEL / Rocky / Alma 8–9 are not supported yet ### Windows Users Download the latest `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows.msi` installer or `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-Portable.zip` portable version from the [Releases](../../releases) page. On Windows on ARM, download `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-arm64.msi` or `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-arm64-Portable.zip`. ### macOS Users **Method 1: Install via Homebrew (Recommended)** ```bash brew install --cask cc-switch ``` Update: ```bash brew upgrade --cask cc-switch ``` **Method 2: Manual Download** Download `CC-Switch-v{version}-macOS.dmg` (recommended) or `.zip` from the [Releases](../../releases) page. It's a Universal build that runs natively on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. > **Note**: CC Switch for macOS is code-signed and notarized by Apple. You can install and open it directly. ### Arch Linux Users **Install via paru (Recommended)** ```bash paru -S cc-switch-bin ``` ### Linux Users Download the latest Linux build from the [Releases](../../releases) page: - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.deb` / `-Linux-arm64.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu) - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.rpm` / `-Linux-arm64.rpm` (Fedora and other RPM distros that ship WebKitGTK 4.1) - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.AppImage` / `-Linux-arm64.AppImage` (any distro meeting the requirements above) > **Flatpak**: Not included in official releases. You can build it yourself from the `.deb` — see [`flatpak/README.md`](flatpak/README.md) for instructions. ## Quick Start ### Basic Usage 1. **Add Provider**: Select the tool you want to manage in the sidebar, then click "+" (Add Provider) in the top-right corner of the page → Choose a preset or create a custom configuration 2. **Switch Provider**: - Main UI: Select provider → Click "Enable" (for OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, MiniMax Code, and Kimi Code the button is "Add", and for Pi and Oh My Pi it's "Enable" / "Remove"; these seven are coexist-mode tools, so you can add several providers at once) - System Tray: One row per tool showing "name · mode · provider · quota"; click a provider name in its submenu to switch (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build) 3. **Takes Effect**: Claude Code needs no restart; for Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build, restart your terminal or the CLI tool; for Claude Desktop, restart the app itself (see FAQ) 4. **Back to Official Login**: Switch to the built-in official provider in the list (e.g. "Claude Official"), restart the tool, then follow its login/OAuth flow 5. **Routing & Aggregation (optional)**: The Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build pages have "Direct" / "Routing" tabs at the top, and Claude Code and Codex also have "Aggregation". Clicking a tab only changes what you're looking at and doesn't touch your configuration; to actually switch, click "Start routing" or "Switch to Aggregation" on the page, and click "Back to direct" to return. Use Routing to use OpenAI- or Gemini-format providers in Claude Code, or Claude in Codex; use Aggregation to mix models from several providers in one model list 6. **Manage Tools**: The "Apps" page in the sidebar shows each AI coding tool's version, install location, and source in one place; you can install, upgrade, or upgrade all, and choose which tools appear in the sidebar ### MCP, Prompts, Skills, Projects & Sessions - **MCP**: Click "MCP" in the sidebar → Add servers via templates or custom config (or "Import Existing") → Toggle sync for each tool - **Prompts**: Click "Prompts" in the sidebar → Create prompts with the Markdown editor → Enable one to write it to that tool's prompt file - **Skills**: Click "Skills" in the sidebar → "Discover Skills" → Search skills.sh or browse GitHub repos → One-click install to supported tools - **Projects**: First turn on "Show project switcher" in "Settings → General", then on the Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or Codex page, open the project switcher at the top → "New project" to save the current configuration; later, pick it from the switcher to switch the whole setup at once - **Sessions**: Click "Sessions" in the sidebar → Browse and search conversation history, open the reading view, or restore each tool's sessions - **Accounts**: Click "Accounts" in the sidebar to sign in to GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, xAI (Grok), and Kimi Code accounts and use your subscriptions as providers. Kimi Code supports multiple official accounts, each with separate credentials and a native provider; the first login uses Kimi's native default credential slot. Manage sign-in, reauthentication and sign-out here. Official Kimi OAuth nodes still present in the native configuration are protected on the provider page; saved profiles can be deleted after their native nodes are removed. > **Note**: On first launch, CC Switch automatically imports your existing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build configuration as a provider named `default` and adds an official provider for each of these tools and Claude Desktop, so nothing you had configured is lost. Which AI tools does CC Switch support? CC Switch supports twelve tools: **Claude Code**, **Claude Desktop**, **Codex**, **Gemini CLI**, **Grok Build**, **OpenCode**, **OpenClaw**, **Hermes**, **Pi**, **MiniMax Code**, **Kimi Code**, **Oh My Pi**. Each tool has dedicated provider presets and configuration management; see [Supported Features by Tool](#supported-features-by-tool) for what each one supports.
Do I need to restart the terminal after switching providers? It depends on the tool: - **Claude Code**: supports hot-switching of provider data — no restart needed. - **Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build**: restart your terminal or the CLI tool for changes to take effect (CC Switch reminds you after switching). In Routing mode, requests go to the new provider immediately, but all three tools may still need a restart if the switch changes the model. - **Aggregation mode**: changes to Claude Code's aggregated models take effect immediately; for Codex, entering or leaving Aggregation and changing the aggregated model list all require a full restart — see the next entry. - **Claude Desktop**: fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop; when using "Model Mapping", also keep CC Switch running. - **OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi, MiniMax Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi**: these are coexist-mode tools — clicking "Add" ("Enable" for Pi and Oh My Pi) writes the provider into the tool's own config alongside the others; you then pick the model you want inside the tool. Kimi Code also provides a "Switch" button to select a provider's model; models still referenced as primary or secondary models cannot be removed. See the [Kimi Code integration guide](docs/kimi-code-integration-zh.md) (Chinese) for configuration and account details.
In Aggregation mode, why don't the aggregated models show up in Codex's /model? Codex reads its model list only at startup. After entering or leaving Aggregation mode, adding or removing an aggregated provider, or changing a provider's aggregated models, fully restart Codex to see the new list: - **Codex CLI**: Closing the terminal and running `codex` again isn't enough. Every `codex` in every terminal shares one background daemon, and it has to be restarted to pick up the new list. When CC Switch detects that Codex is still using the old list, it shows a notice at the top of the Codex page; click "Restart Codex daemon" in the notice. Restarting interrupts any tasks running in the daemon. - **Codex desktop app**: Quit it completely and reopen it (press ⌘Q on macOS; closing the window isn't enough). - **Editor extensions**: Reopen the editor window. Claude Code isn't affected: changes to aggregated models take effect immediately.
Will switching providers change my plugins, hooks, or other settings? No. When you switch providers for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Grok Build, CC Switch replaces only the **key fields** in the config file: the endpoint, key, model name, and API protocol (plus the reasoning effort for Codex and the auth method for Gemini CLI), along with a few compatibility options that belong to the provider (such as Claude Code's "Disable Artifact Tool" and the context window). Plugins, hooks, permissions, MCP, environment variables you added yourself, comments, and formatting all stay as they are and apply to every provider. You can change these shared settings in the tool itself or by editing the config file by hand. You can also edit any provider in CC Switch: the editor shows "what the config file will look like after switching to this provider". When you save, the key fields are stored in that provider, and every other change is written to the config file and applies to every provider. So the old "Common Config Snippet" is no longer needed, and its buttons have been removed. Settings that were in your snippet before the upgrade were already written into the config file when you switched, so they stay. Before CC Switch rewrites each config file for the first time, it also backs up the original to `~/.cc-switch/backups/live-first-write/`.
I changed the model inside the tool — why does it go back after I switch away and back? The model is a key field and belongs to the provider. A model you pick inside the tool (such as with `/model` in Claude Code) stays in effect until the next switch; when you switch, the model in the config file is replaced with the one saved in the target provider, and CC Switch doesn't save the model you picked back to the previous provider. To keep using a model long-term, edit that provider in CC Switch. Older versions saved the whole config file back to the provider when you switched away. That no longer happens: it froze plugins and other shared settings into one provider, so they were lost when you switched to another one.
Why can't I delete the provider currently in use? CC Switch follows a "minimal intrusion" design principle — even if you uninstall the app, your tools will continue to work normally. So for tools that use one active provider at a time (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build), the system always keeps one configuration in use, because deleting all configurations would make the corresponding tool unusable; to delete it, switch to another provider first. Likewise, the default provider in Aggregation mode can't be removed; make another provider the default first. Coexist-mode tools (OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi, and MiniMax Code) aren't subject to this restriction — you can delete any provider directly. If you rarely use a tool, you can hide it from the sidebar on the "Apps" page. To switch back to official login, see the next question.
How do I switch back to official login? In CC Switch, the provider lists for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build each include a built-in official provider (**Claude Official**, **Claude Desktop Official**, **OpenAI Official**, **Google Official**, **Grok Official**); if you deleted it, add it back from the presets. After switching to the official provider, follow the tool's own login flow (e.g. `/login` in Claude Code, `codex login` for Codex), and then you can freely switch between the official provider and third-party providers. For Codex, you can also sign in to multiple ChatGPT accounts inside CC Switch via "Sign in with ChatGPT" and choose an "Account to use" for each **OpenAI Official** card, so switching between multiple Plus, Pro, or Team accounts takes one click; cards set to "Follow Codex login" keep using the Codex CLI's own login. Note: official subscriptions use the tool's own login and don't go through local routing. Official providers can't be selected in Routing mode (Codex's OpenAI Official cards are the exception); switch back to Direct first.
After I start routing, why does my config file point to 127.0.0.1? In Routing mode, the tool's requests first go to CC Switch's local routing (`http://127.0.0.1:15721` by default), and CC Switch then forwards them to the provider you selected. That's why the tool's config file only contains the local address and the placeholder key `PROXY_MANAGED`; for Claude Code, the model name is also written as a fixed alias such as `claude-sonnet-5` (the `/model` menu still shows the real model name). The real provider address, key, and model are all stored in CC Switch. Aggregation mode works the same way. In the request logs under "Usage" in the sidebar, you can see "requested model → actual model" for each request. In Routing mode, switching changes the provider that routing uses; the provider you were using before you entered Routing stays the same and is labeled "Direct" on its card. When you click "Back to direct", the config file is written back to this direct provider's configuration. Quitting CC Switch also writes back the direct provider first, and it reconnects the next time CC Switch starts.
Can I use OpenAI-compatible APIs, Gemini, or local models in Claude Code? Yes, but you need to use Routing. When editing the provider, set "Upstream Format" under "Advanced Options" to match the provider's API: choose "OpenAI Chat Completions" for services that only offer a Chat Completions endpoint (as many local model servers do), "OpenAI Responses API" for services that offer a Responses endpoint, and "Gemini Native generateContent" for Gemini. Then click "Start routing" on the "Routing" tab of the Claude Code page. Choosing the wrong format or not starting routing usually results in a 404 or 405 error. Conversely, choosing "Anthropic Messages" as the "Upstream Format" in Codex or Grok Build lets you use Claude-format providers; this also requires Routing. See [Using GPT in Claude Code](docs/guides/claude-codex-routing-guide-en.md) and [Using Claude in Codex](docs/guides/codex-claude-routing-guide-en.md) for details.
"Connectivity check" passed, so why do requests still fail? The "Connectivity check" on a provider card only checks whether the provider address is reachable; it doesn't send a real model request, so it can't verify whether the API key and model name are correct. When requests fail, check the key, model name, and upstream format; for requests that go through Routing, you can also see the exact error in the request logs under "Usage" in the sidebar.
Where is my data stored? By default, everything is stored in the `.cc-switch` folder in your home directory (`C:\Users\\.cc-switch` on Windows): - **Database**: `cc-switch.db` (SQLite — providers, MCP, prompts, Skills, projects, usage records, etc.) - **Local settings**: `settings.json` (device-level settings such as each tool's config directory, backup policy, and cloud sync connection details) - **Backups**: `backups/` (backed up automatically every 24 hours by default, keeping the 10 most recent; adjustable in "Settings → Data → Backup & Restore"; "Other Backups" below it lists the location and size of every other backup, which you can clean up by category) - **Skills**: `skills/` (can be changed to `~/.agents/skills` in Settings), synced to each tool via symlinks by default, falling back to copying if that fails - **Skill Backups**: `skill-backups/` (created automatically before uninstalling or updating a skill, keeping the 20 most recent) - **OAuth login credentials**: `copilot_auth.json`, `codex_oauth_auth.json`, `xai_oauth_auth.json` - **Logs**: `logs/cc-switch.log` and `crash.log` — please attach them when reporting an issue - **Device state**: `live-state.json` (whether each tool is currently in Direct, Routing, or Aggregation mode, and what was last written), `codex-login-stash.json` (the official Codex login moved aside when you switch to a third-party provider, restored when you switch back to an official one) - **Original config files**: `backups/live-first-write/` (each tool's config file as it was before CC Switch first rewrote it) After you change "CC Switch Configuration Directory" in "Settings → Data → Location", all of the files above except `settings.json`, the device state, and the original config files are stored in the new directory. CC Switch doesn't move existing files automatically, so copy them over manually first. `settings.json`, the device state, and the original config files belong to this computer only: they always stay in the default directory and are not included in cloud sync.
How do I manage tools inside WSL on Windows? CC Switch doesn't detect WSL automatically. In "Settings → App config", change the config directory for the corresponding tool to a path inside WSL, e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\\.claude`; after you save, CC Switch reads and writes the config inside WSL (supported for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, and Pi). Once this is set, the "Apps" page in the sidebar also detects and upgrades that tool in the corresponding WSL distribution. Note: Routing and Aggregation write `127.0.0.1` as the address into the config. In WSL2's default NAT networking mode, `127.0.0.1` inside WSL can't reach local routing on Windows; switch WSL to mirrored networking mode instead.
Is there a command-line or headless version? CC Switch itself only ships as a desktop app that requires a graphical interface (see [Download & Installation](#download--installation) for system requirements). For servers, SSH sessions, or machines without a desktop environment, we recommend the community-maintained **[CC Switch CLI](https://github.com/SaladDay/cc-switch-cli)**: it offers both an interactive terminal UI (TUI) and a command-line mode, supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, and Pi, and can be installed via Homebrew (`brew install cc-switch-cli`) or an install script. By default, CC Switch CLI shares the `~/.cc-switch` data directory with the desktop app and is compatible with the desktop app's WebDAV sync. The two projects are released separately, and the database version the CLI supports sometimes lags behind the desktop app; if you see a "database version is too new" message, upgrade the CLI or wait for it to catch up.
Linux (Wayland + NVIDIA): clicks don't register and the window black-screens on resize The AppImage forces `GDK_BACKEND=x11` (XWayland) to avoid a historical native-Wayland crash. On newer Wayland + NVIDIA setups this can leave the web content area unclickable (the title-bar buttons still work) and black-screen on resize. Launch with the opt-in escape hatch to switch back to native Wayland: ```bash CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=wayland ./CC-Switch-*.AppImage ``` If you launch from a desktop icon, add it to the `.desktop` `Exec=` line (e.g. `env CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=wayland /path/to/AppImage`) or set it in your session environment. The variable is generic: on tiling Wayland compositors (sway/Hyprland) where clicks don't register, try `CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=x11` instead. Leaving it unset keeps the default behavior.

## 下載與安裝 ### 系統需求 - **Windows**：Windows 10 及以上 - **macOS**：macOS 12（Monterey）及以上 - **Linux**：x86_64 或 ARM64，glibc 2.35+ 並具備 WebKitGTK 4.1——例如 Ubuntu 22.04+、Debian 12+ 與較新的 Fedora 版本；尚不支援 RHEL / Rocky / Alma 8–9 ### Windows 使用者 請從 [Releases](../../releases) 頁面下載最新的 `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows.msi` 安裝程式，或 `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-Portable.zip` 免安裝版。若是 Windows on ARM，請下載 `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-arm64.msi` 或 `CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows-arm64-Portable.zip`。 ### macOS 使用者 **方式一：透過 Homebrew 安裝（建議）** ```bash brew install --cask cc-switch ``` 更新： ```bash brew upgrade --cask cc-switch ``` **方式二：手動下載** 從 [Releases](../../releases) 頁面下載 `CC-Switch-v{version}-macOS.dmg`（建議）或 `.zip`。這是 Universal 版本，可在 Apple Silicon 與 Intel Mac 上原生執行。 > **注意**：macOS 版 CC Switch 已通過程式碼簽署並經 Apple 公證，可直接安裝並開啟。 ### Arch Linux 使用者 **透過 paru 安裝（建議）** ```bash paru -S cc-switch-bin ``` ### Linux 使用者 請從 [Releases](../../releases) 頁面下載最新的 Linux 版本： - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.deb` / `-Linux-arm64.deb`（Debian/Ubuntu） - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.rpm` / `-Linux-arm64.rpm`（Fedora 及其他附帶 WebKitGTK 4.1 的 RPM 發行版） - `CC-Switch-v{version}-Linux-x86_64.AppImage` / `-Linux-arm64.AppImage`（任何符合上述需求的發行版） > **Flatpak**：官方發行版不提供。你可以自行從 `.deb` 建置——步驟請見 [`flatpak/README.md`](flatpak/README.md)。 ## 快速開始 ### 基本使用 1. **新增供應商**：在側欄選擇要管理的工具，然後點擊頁面右上角的「+」（新增供應商）→ 選擇預設或建立自訂設定 2. **切換供應商**： - CC Switch 支援哪些 AI 工具？ CC Switch 支援十二個工具：**Claude Code**、**Claude Desktop**、**Codex**、**Gemini CLI**、**Grok Build**、**OpenCode**、**OpenClaw**、**Hermes**、**Pi**、**MiniMax Code**、**Kimi Code**、**Oh My Pi**。每個工具都有專屬的供應商預設與設定管理；各工具支援的功能請見[各工具支援的功能](#各工具支援的功能)。
切換供應商後需要重新啟動終端機嗎？ 視工具而定： - **Claude Code**：支援供應商資料熱切換，無需重新啟動。 - **Codex、Gemini CLI、Grok Build**：請重新啟動終端機或 CLI 工具，變更才會生效（切換後 CC Switch 會提醒你）。在路由模式下，請求會立即送往新的供應商，但若切換會更動模型，這三個工具仍可能需要重新啟動。 - **聚合模式**：Claude Code 聚合模型的變更會立即生效；Codex 進入或離開聚合、以及變更聚合模型清單，都需要完整重新啟動——見下一則。 - **Claude Desktop**：完全結束並重新開啟 Claude Desktop；使用「模型映射」時，也請保持 CC Switch 執行中。 - **OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes、Pi、MiniMax Code、Kimi Code、Oh My Pi**：這些是共存式工具——點擊「新增」（Pi 與 Oh My Pi 為「啟用」）會把供應商與其他供應商一起寫入工具自己的設定；之後再到工具內選擇你要的模型。Kimi Code 還提供「切換」按鈕來選擇供應商的模型；仍被設為主要或次要模型的模型無法移除。設定與帳號詳情請見 [Kimi Code 整合指南](docs/kimi-code-integration-zh.md)（中文）。
聚合模式下，為什麼聚合的模型沒有出現在 Codex 的 /model 中？ Codex 只會在啟動時讀取模型清單。進入或離開聚合模式、新增或移除聚合供應商，或變更供應商的聚合模型後，請完整重新啟動 Codex 才能看到新的清單： - **Codex CLI**：關閉終端機再執行 `codex` 並不夠。所有終端機中的每個 `codex` 共用同一個背景常駐程式，必須重新啟動它才會讀取新的清單。當 CC Switch 偵測到 Codex 仍在使用舊清單時，會在 Codex 頁面頂端顯示提示；請點擊提示中的「重新啟動 Codex 守護行程」。重新啟動會中斷常駐程式中正在執行的任何任務。 - **Codex 桌面應用程式**：完全結束後重新開啟（在 macOS 上按 ⌘Q；只關閉視窗並不夠）。 - **編輯器擴充功能**：重新開啟編輯器視窗。 Claude Code 不受影響：聚合模型的變更會立即生效。
切換供應商會更動我的外掛、Hook 或其他設定嗎？ 不會。為 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 或 Grok Build 切換供應商時，CC Switch 只會替換設定檔中的**關鍵欄位**：端點、金鑰、模型名稱與 API 協定（Codex 另含推理強度，Gemini CLI 另含驗證方式），以及少數屬於供應商的相容性選項（例如 Claude Code 的「停用 Artifact 工具」與上下文視窗）。外掛、Hook、權限、MCP、你自己加入的環境變數、註解與格式都保持原樣，並適用於每個供應商。 你可以在工具本身或手動編輯設定檔來變更這些共用設定。你也可以在 CC Switch 中編輯任一供應商：編輯器會顯示「切換到此供應商後設定檔的樣子」。儲存時，關鍵欄位會存入該供應商，其餘所有變更則寫入設定檔，並適用於每個供應商。 因此舊有的「通用設定片段」已不再需要，其按鈕也已移除。升級前在片段中的設定，早在你切換時就已寫入設定檔，所以會保留下來。CC Switch 在第一次改寫每個設定檔之前，也會把原始檔案備份到 `~/.cc-switch/backups/live-first-write/`。
我在工具內改了模型，為什麼切換走再切換回來後又變回去了？ 模型是關鍵欄位，屬於供應商。你在工具內選擇的模型（例如在 Claude Code 中使用 `/model`）會一直生效到下次切換；切換時，設定檔中的模型會被替換成目標供應商中儲存的模型，而 CC Switch 不會把你選擇的模型存回前一個供應商。若想長期使用某個模型，請在 CC Switch 中編輯該供應商。 舊版本在你切換離開時，會把整個設定檔存回供應商。現在已不再這樣做：那會把外掛與其他共用設定凍結在單一供應商中，切換到別的供應商時就會遺失。
為什麼無法刪除目前使用中的供應商？ CC Switch 遵循「最小侵入」的設計原則——即使你解除安裝本應用程式，你的工具仍能正常運作。 因此，對於同一時間只使用一個供應商的工具（Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、Gemini CLI、Grok Build），系統一律會保留一份使用中的設定，因為刪除所有設定會讓對應的工具無法使用；若要刪除，請先切換到其他供應商。同樣地，聚合模式的預設供應商也無法移除；請先將另一個供應商設為預設。共存式工具（OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes、Pi 與 MiniMax Code）不受此限制——你可以直接刪除任何供應商。如果你很少使用某個工具，可以在「應用」頁面將它從側欄隱藏。若要切換回官方登入，請見下一個問題。
如何切換回官方登入？ 在 CC Switch 中，Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、Gemini CLI 與 Grok Build 的供應商清單各自包含一個內建的官方供應商（**Claude Official**、**Claude Desktop Official**、**OpenAI Official**、**Google Official**、**Grok Official**）；如果你刪除了它，可以從預設中重新新增。切換到官方供應商後，請依照工具自己的登入流程操作（例如 Claude Code 的 `/login`、Codex 的 `codex login`），之後你就能在官方供應商與第三方供應商之間自由切換。 對於 Codex，你也可以在 CC Switch 內透過「Sign in with ChatGPT」登入多個 ChatGPT 帳號，並為每張 **OpenAI Official** 卡片選擇「使用的帳號」，只需一鍵就能在多個 Plus、Pro 或 Team 帳號之間切換；設為「跟隨 Codex 登入」的卡片則會繼續使用 Codex CLI 自己的登入。 注意：官方訂閱使用工具自己的登入，不會經過本地路由。路由模式下無法選擇官方供應商（Codex 的 OpenAI Official 卡片除外）；請先切換回直連。
開始路由後，為什麼我的設定檔指向 127.0.0.1？ 在路由模式下，工具的請求會先送到 CC Switch 的本地路由（預設為 `http://127.0.0.1:15721`），再由 CC Switch 轉發給你選擇的供應商。因此工具的設定檔裡只會有本機位址與預留位置金鑰 `PROXY_MANAGED`；對於 Claude Code，模型名稱也會寫成固定的別名，例如 `claude-sonnet-5`（`/model` 選單仍會顯示真實的模型名稱）。真實的供應商位址、金鑰與模型都儲存在 CC Switch 中。聚合模式的運作方式相同。 在側欄「用量統計」的請求日誌中，你可以看到每個請求的「請求的模型 → 實際的模型」。 在路由模式下，切換改變的是路由所使用的供應商；你在進入路由之前使用的供應商維持不變，並在其卡片上標示為「直連」。當你點擊「回到直連」時，設定檔會被寫回這個直連供應商的設定。結束 CC Switch 時也會先寫回直連供應商，並在下次啟動 CC Switch 時重新接上。
可以在 Claude Code 中使用 OpenAI 相容 API、Gemini 或本地模型嗎？ 可以，但需要使用路由。編輯供應商時，請將「進階選項」中的「上游格式」設為與供應商 API 相符：只提供 Chat Completions 端點的服務（許多本地模型伺服器都是如此）請選「OpenAI Chat Completions」，提供 Responses 端點的服務請選「OpenAI Responses API」，Gemini 請選「Gemini Native generateContent」。然後在 Claude Code 頁面的「路由」分頁點擊「開始路由」。選錯格式或沒有開始路由，通常會出現 404 或 405 錯誤。 反過來說，在 Codex 或 Grok Build 中將「上游格式」選為「Anthropic Messages」，就能使用 Claude 格式的供應商；這同樣需要路由。詳情請見[在 Claude Code 中使用 GPT](docs/guides/claude-codex-routing-guide-en.md)與[在 Codex 中使用 Claude](docs/guides/codex-claude-routing-guide-en.md)。
「檢測連通」通過了，為什麼請求還是失敗？ 供應商卡片上的「檢測連通」只會檢查供應商位址是否可連線，並不會送出真正的模型請求，因此無法驗證 API 金鑰與模型名稱是否正確。請求失敗時，請檢查金鑰、模型名稱與上游格式；對於經過路由的請求，你也可以在側欄「用量統計」的請求日誌中看到確切的錯誤。
我的資料存放在哪裡？ 預設情況下，所有資料都存放在你使用者主目錄下的 `.cc-switch` 資料夾（Windows 上為 `C:\Users\\.cc-switch`）： - **資料庫**：`cc-switch.db`（SQLite——供應商、MCP、提示詞、Skills、專案、用量記錄等） - **本機設定**：`settings.json`（裝置層級的設定，例如各工具的設定目錄、備份策略與雲端同步連線資訊） - **備份**：`backups/`（預設每 24 小時自動備份一次，保留最近 10 份；可在「設定 → 資料 → 備份與還原」中調整；其下的「其他備份」會列出其他所有備份的位置與大小，可依類別清理） - **Skills**：`skills/`（可在設定中改為 `~/.agents/skills`），預設透過符號連結同步到各工具，失敗時退回複製 - **Skill 備份**：`skill-backups/`（在解除安裝或更新 Skill 之前自動建立，保留最近 20 份） - **OAuth 登入憑證**：`copilot_auth.json`、`codex_oauth_auth.json`、`xai_oauth_auth.json` - **日誌**：`logs/cc-switch.log` 與 `crash.log`——回報問題時請附上 - **裝置狀態**：`live-state.json`（各工具目前處於直連、路由或聚合模式，以及最後寫入的內容）、`codex-login-stash.json`（切換到第三方供應商時暫存起來的 Codex 官方登入，切換回官方供應商時會還原） - **原始設定檔**：`backups/live-first-write/`（CC Switch 第一次改寫之前各工具設定檔的原樣） 在「設定 → 資料 → 儲存位置」中變更「CC Switch 設定目錄」後，除了 `settings.json`、裝置狀態與原始設定檔之外，上述所有檔案都會存放在新目錄中。CC Switch 不會自動搬移既有檔案，請先手動複製過去。`settings.json`、裝置狀態與原始設定檔只屬於這台電腦：它們一律保留在預設目錄，也不會納入雲端同步。
如何在 Windows 上管理 WSL 內的工具？ CC Switch 不會自動偵測 WSL。請在「設定 → 應用設定」中，把對應工具的設定目錄改成 WSL 內的路徑，例如 `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\\.claude`；儲存後，CC Switch 就會讀寫 WSL 內的設定（支援 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、Grok Build、OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes 與 Pi）。設定完成後，側欄的「應用」頁面也會偵測並升級對應 WSL 發行版中的該工具。 注意：路由與聚合會把 `127.0.0.1` 作為位址寫入設定。在 WSL2 預設的 NAT 網路模式下，WSL 內的 `127.0.0.1` 無法連到 Windows 上的本地路由；請改將 WSL 切換為鏡像網路模式。
有命令列或無頭（headless）版本嗎？ CC Switch 本身只以需要圖形介面的桌面應用程式形式發行（系統需求請見[下載與安裝](#下載與安裝)）。對於伺服器、SSH 連線或沒有桌面環境的機器，我們建議使用社群維護的 **[CC Switch CLI](https://github.com/SaladDay/cc-switch-cli)**：它同時提供互動式終端機介面（TUI）與命令列模式，支援 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes 與 Pi，並可透過 Homebrew（`brew install cc-switch-cli`）或安裝指令碼安裝。 預設情況下，CC Switch CLI 與桌面應用程式共用 `~/.cc-switch` 資料目錄，並相容桌面應用程式的 WebDAV 同步。這兩個專案是分開發布的，CLI 支援的資料庫版本有時會落後於桌面應用程式；若你看到「資料庫版本過新」的訊息，請升級 CLI，或等待它跟上。
Linux（Wayland + NVIDIA）：點擊沒有反應，且調整視窗大小時黑屏 AppImage 會強制設定 `GDK_BACKEND=x11`（XWayland），以避開過去原生 Wayland 的當機問題。在較新的 Wayland + NVIDIA 環境中，這可能導致網頁內容區域無法點擊（標題列按鈕仍可使用），並在調整大小時黑屏。請使用選擇性啟用的逃生開關啟動，以切換回原生 Wayland： ```bash CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=wayland ./CC-Switch-*.AppImage ``` 如果你是從桌面圖示啟動，請把它加到 `.desktop` 檔的 `Exec=` 行（例如 `env CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=wayland /path/to/AppImage`），或設定在你的工作階段環境中。這個變數是通用的：在點擊沒有反應的平鋪式 Wayland 合成器（sway/Hyprland）上，請改試 `CC_SWITCH_GDK_BACKEND=x11`。不設定則維持預設行為。
